newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE CAN'T AFFORD TO GIVE IN TO FARMERS, PAPOUTSIS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE CAN'T AFFORD TO GIVE IN TO FARMERS, PAPOUTSIS.

text.p: The Greek economy cannot afford to meet the 'groundless and dangerous' demands of farmers, Greece's European Commissioner Christos Papoutsis was reported as saying in the Athens daily 'Ta Nea'.

"Groundless demands and proposals which are dangerous for the whole of the country's economy have easily turned into slogans," he said in an interview. "They cannot however be realised when the country and the economy are bound by international agreements."

Papoutsis, in charge of trade, small and medium-size enterprises and tourism, said the farmers' demands for the abolition of the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs and the EU's Common Agricultural Policy were "irresponsible and dangerous".
He said such moves would be disastrous for EU countries of the South.

"There are more voices calling for the abolition of CAP and the 'renationalisation' of farming policies, in order for Community funds now going to the countries of the South - and particularly Greece - to be redirected to the candidate countries of Central and Eastern Europe," he said.
Papoutsis said the government had to "tell farmers the truth" and go ahead with reforms in farming methods, production and trade to make the Greek farm product more competitive.
